newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel PM said seeking economic plan by year end.
newsitem.headline: Israel PM said seeking economic plan by year end.

text.p: The Israeli government will unveil a wide-ranging economic programme after approval of the 1997 budget, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told the head of the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce.

Federation president Danny Gillerman quoted Netanyahu as saying the plan would include a new long-term monetary policy, capital market reform, a comprehensive privatisation programme and stepped-up tenders of state-owned land for development.
The government is scheduled to present the 1997 budget to parliament on October 29 for approval by the end of the year.
There have been periodic rumours that the government is planning a comprehensive economic programme that would include an easing of monetary policy by the Bank of Israel.
In the meantime, Netanyahu has promised to announce a privatisation programme in November and the cabinet is now weighing a package of capital market reforms presented by the Treasury.
Gillerman sharply attacked the central bank, which he said had hoped to contain inflation at little cost to the economy.
"Instead, we've gotten a series of crises in different sectors of the economy, the worst being in export, construction and the capital markets," Gillerman said.
